newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr rise above 110 yen no big worry - Japan sources.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rise above 110 yen no big worry - Japan sources.

text.p: Japan does not think a dollar rise above 110 yen would be a big problem, government sources said on Friday.
The government had no inflation worries and a weaker yen should not have much negative impact on the economy, the sources said.
They said they also believed the U.S. government wanted a stronger dollar to boost investments, and that worries U.S. exporters would lose their competitive edge concerned only certain industries.

"If the dollar rises beyond 110 yen...I don't think it would be an especially big problem, but we have no intention of pushing up the dollar intentionally. We hope the currency market moves in a stable manner," a government source said.
The comments are at odds with recent private-sector remarks in the United States.

One of the biggest U.S. industries affected by exchange rates is the car sector, and when the dollar peaked at 111.19 yen on July 8, officials from the "Big Three" U.S. carmakers made repeated trips to Washington to complain, saying the rising dollar was hindering exports.
The sources said currency markets had moved in a stable manner recently and should not be a major issue at a meeting of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers expected later this month in Washington.
One government source said it was possible Washington would ask Japan to come up with an additional fiscal spending plan for the current fiscal year to stimulate the economy.
However, current economic conditions in Japan did not necessarily warrant a supplementary budget featuring large public works projects, he said.
The source also mentioned that cutting the state deficit was a global trend and that Japan was unlikely to be pressed to do something for the economy from the fiscal side.
